title: UCINET .uci dataset, schema version 1.0
description: A single-file JSON replacement for the ##h/##d pair (SPEC D6). One file holds everything the pair did - the matrices, the labels, the mode, the directedness, the multi-relation stack, the title - plus node attributes and provenance, which the old format had no room for. Written to be implementable in Delphi XE7's System.JSON as well as in R: the structure is deliberately shallow, every array is homogeneous, and nothing depends on key order. Draft for review; nothing outside xucinet reads it yet.

uci.description: Schema version of this file, not the version of the program that wrote it. A reader should refuse a major version it does not know.

title.description: Dataset name, as the ##h header's title field carried it. Printed reports use it to name the input.

mode.description: 1-mode when rows and columns are the same node set, 2-mode when they are not. Not inferred from squareness: a 1-mode network can be square by coincidence and a 2-mode one can be square by accident.

directed.description: true, false, or null when it is not determined. Null is the honest value for 2-mode data, where directedness has no meaning.

rowlabels.description: One label per row. Omit the key entirely if the file carries no labels; a reader then supplies 1..nrows, as UCINET does. An empty array is not the same thing and is not allowed.

collabels.description: One label per column. Same rule as rowlabels. For 1-mode data these normally repeat rowlabels rather than being omitted, so that a reader need not special-case them.

datatype.description: Hint for a writer converting back to ##h/##d, which must choose a fixed cell width. Values are the names from ucommon.pas. Purely advisory: the numbers in this file are exact regardless, and a reader that ignores this key loses nothing.

relations.description: The matrices, in stack order. A single-relation dataset has one entry. Every relation is nrows by ncols and shares the labels above; that is what makes the stack a stack.

name.description: Relation name, from the ##h matrix labels. Sampson's ten arrive as SAMPLK1 .. SAMPNPR.

layout.description: How the payload below is written. 'matrix' is dense, 'edgelist' is sparse. The words are the ones the R interface already uses for input layouts, deliberately, so users meet one vocabulary rather than two.

values.description: For layout 'matrix', nrows arrays of ncols numbers, row-major, matching the ##d file's own order. For layout 'edgelist', one number per entry in i and j. A missing cell is JSON null, never a sentinel: the 1e37/1e38 convention stays inside the binary format where it belongs, and a reader writing back to ##d restores it.

i.description: Row indices for layout 'edgelist', 1-based. Cells not listed are zero. To record a missing cell in a sparse relation, list it with a null value.

attributes.description: Node attributes, which the ##h/##d pair could only hold as a separate dataset. Optional. Keyed by label rather than by position so that a reader can align them to the network even if either has been reordered.

rows.description: The node each row of every variable belongs to. Normally equal to rowlabels, but need not be: a 2-mode dataset may carry attributes for its column mode instead.

values.description: One value per entry in rows. Numbers, or null where missing. Strings are allowed for genuinely categorical attributes that have no numeric coding.

provenance.description: Who wrote the file and from what. Advisory, ignored on read, and never load-bearing - but the reason a dataset five years from now can be traced to the file it came from.

source.description: What this was converted from, if anything, e.g. 'campnet.##h'.
